bug_semantics: Unauthenticated Meteor method sendForgotPasswordEmail is reachable over DDP and POST /api/v1/method.callAnon/sendForgotPasswordEmail with no dedicated DDPRateLimiter rule. A caller can invoke it unbounded, which (1) drives an unlimited volume of password-reset mail from the deployment sender at any address that matches an account, and (2) distinguishes account classes from the boolean return: true when the address has no account or a reset is sent, false when the address is an OAuth-only account and Accounts_AllowPasswordChangeForOAuthUsers is off (CWE-307 / CWE-204). The REST users.forgotPassword path is separately bounded; the DDP method was not.
flaw_origin: The smallest first write is Rodrigo Nascimento's 2015-05-24 commit that added server/methods/sendForgotPasswordEmail.coffee: an unauthenticated Meteor.methods handler that looks up the user, sends Accounts.sendResetPasswordEmail, and returns true/false, with no DDPRateLimiter.addRule. Later Coffee-to-JS, monorepo, and folder moves preserved that unprotected method. Return semantics later changed (2020 anti-enumeration true-for-missing; 2020/2024 OAuth-only false), but the missing per-method DDP rate limit and unauthenticated reset-mail send date to that first registration. Parent 1f072dfa6ae3cc06fb9d6abd5c9422ffdd1a5efc has no sendForgotPasswordEmail / sendResetPasswordEmail.

Fix 3a61c3afed2df5d1555282e496e9f854c9e69916 (Julio Araujo, GitHub squash of PR #41699, parent 18f5eb45d098ca64d403fdae4704211000efba29) adds DDPRateLimiter.addRule({type:'method', name:'sendForgotPasswordEmail', clientAddress(){return true}}, 10, 60000). PR #41699 notes the generic per-connection DDP limiter can be bypassed via extra connections; the new rule is per clientAddress. Advisory patch URL is https://github.com/RocketChat/Rocket.Chat/commit/3a61c3afe.

reasoning: CVE-2026-75575 / GHSA-jfh6-w7r2-rj74 is a real published issue (not withdrawn): sendForgotPasswordEmail is an unauthenticated DDP method without a dedicated DDPRateLimiter rule, enabling reset-mail flooding and boolean probing of OAuth-only accounts. The fix in PR #41699 / 3a61c3afed2df5d1555282e496e9f854c9e69916 only adds a 10/min per-clientAddress rule; it does not change return values. The BIC is therefore the smallest commit that first registered that unprotected method. git log -S / --diff-filter=A plus parent-tree grep show that is 063bb185131539f2d309abd5d599add22e3989e9 (2015-05-24), which added the CoffeeScript Meteor.methods handler with true/false user-existence returns and reset-mail send. The parent tree lacks the method. Later conversions and moves are not BICs; the 2020/2024 return-value edits refined CWE-204 but did not introduce the missing rate limit the advisory and patch address, and CNA affected-from-0 requires a BIC at product origin.
